The sibling file `curriculumEnricher.ts` (lines 193-209) demonstrates the correct pattern: wrap the risky step in try/catch, set `status: 'failed'` with an error message, then rethrow. `curriculumBuilder.ts` omits this entirely.
findings.impact: The client polls GET /ai-curriculum/build-status/:jobId expecting status to eventually become 'completed' or 'failed' (routes-ai-curriculum-builder.ts:651-655 doc comment). On any generation failure the job is stuck at 'building' indefinitely — the polling UI shows a perpetual progress spinner with no way to know the build failed, and DELETE /ai-curriculum/build/:jobId is the only way out (requires the user to notice and manually cancel).
findings.recommendation: Wrap the `generate-curriculum` step (and ideally the whole function body) in try/catch; on error, update `curriculumBuildJobs` to `status: 'failed', error: <message>` before rethrowing — mirroring the exact pattern already used in curriculumEnricher.ts.

findings.title: Two functions named stripCodeFences with different, non-equivalent behavior — the weaker one guards the highest-stakes AI parse
findings.detail: `routes-ai-curriculum-builder.ts:578-583` defines `stripCodeFences` using anchored regex (`^```...`, `...```$`) that only strips fences at the exact start/end of the string. `src/lib/import/helpers.ts:413-420` defines a different `stripCodeFences` with an explicit comment: 'Strip markdown code fences from AI response, including when preamble text precedes the fence' — using a non-anchored match specifically to handle cases like 'Here is the JSON: ```json {...} ```'. `routes-ai-curriculum-incremental.ts` imports and uses the robust helpers.ts version; but `curriculumBuilder.ts` (the Inngest job doing the single largest, most expensive 32000-token curriculum generation) imports and uses the weaker builder.ts version.
findings.impact: If Claude prepends any conversational preamble before the JSON code fence in the full one-shot curriculum build (more likely on the largest/most complex generations, which is exactly this endpoint), the weaker `stripCodeFences` leaves the preamble text in the string, `safeParseAIJson` fails to parse it, and the build fails — a failure mode the codebase already solved for the import path but did not carry over to the builder path.
findings.recommendation: Delete the weaker duplicate in routes-ai-curriculum-builder.ts and have all curriculum-builder consumers import the robust version from lib/import/helpers.ts (already done correctly in routes-ai-curriculum-incremental.ts).

findings.title: Autosave failure in curriculum-detail.tsx is silent — violates the project's own documented anti-pattern
findings.detail: In the debounced autosave effect (lines 996-1037), when the PUT to `/curriculum/:id/detail` returns `!res.ok` (line 1020-1024), the code does `console.error(...)` and `return` — no `toast.error`, no UI state change, nothing visible to the user. Compare to `handleVersionModalConfirm` (lines 1064-1074) which correctly calls `toast.error` on the same failure condition against the same endpoint.
findings.impact: A user editing a locked, high-value curriculum (PDD-009 surface) can have their in-progress edits silently fail to persist — e.g. after a transient 5xx, an auth session hiccup, or a payload validation rejection — while the UI shows no error. The user believes the curriculum is saved; a page refresh or another admin's concurrent load will show stale/lost data. This directly matches the exact anti-pattern the project's CLAUDE.md calls out under 'Silent Catch Blocks Prohibited' (though that section is written for empty-list fetches, the underlying principle — user must be told when a save silently fails — applies squarely here).
findings.recommendation: Add `toast.error('Failed to save changes — please retry')` (and consider a persistent 'unsaved changes' indicator) in the `!res.ok` branch at line 1020-1024, matching the explicit-save handler's behavior.

findings.title: generate-stage endpoint checks org membership but not build ownership — any org user can drive another user's incremental build
findings.detail: POST /ai-curriculum/incremental/:buildId/generate-stage (lines 556-664), GET /ai-curriculum/incremental/:buildId (lines 465-488), and POST .../approve-outline and .../approve-stage all filter the build lookup only by `eq(curriculumIncrementalBuilds.id, buildId)` + `eq(..., flightSchoolId, orgId)` — they never check `eq(..., userId, authUser.id)`. Only the DELETE endpoint (lines 813-834) additionally scopes by `userId`. Since builds are per-user, drafty, in-progress state (start.ts explicitly cancels 'any existing in-progress builds for this location+user' to avoid orphans, implying builds are meant to be user-scoped), any authenticated user within the same flight school/org can view, drive stage generation for, approve stages into, and publish another user's in-progress incremental curriculum build by guessing/enumerating its UUID buildId.
findings.impact: Cross-user interference within the same org: one instructor/admin could inadvertently (or via a leaked/logged buildId) advance, approve-into, or publish another user's WIP curriculum draft, consuming their AI budget and potentially publishing content the original author never reviewed.
findings.recommendation: Add `eq(curriculumIncrementalBuilds.userId, authUser.id)` to the WHERE clause on all incremental build routes that currently only check orgId, consistent with the DELETE route's existing pattern — or make an explicit product decision that these are org-shared drafts and document it.

findings.title: generate-stage does not validate stageIdx lower bound — negative index causes undefined stage crash
findings.detail: Line 595-598: `const stageIdx = body.stageIdx ?? build.currentStageIdx; if (stageIdx >= outline.stages.length) return 400;` — only the upper bound is checked. A caller passing `stageIdx: -1` (or any negative integer) passes this guard, then `outline.stages[stageIdx]` at line 600 evaluates to `undefined`, and `targetStage.name` on line 611 (via buildStagePrompt call) throws a TypeError, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 400.
findings.impact: Low-severity crash/500 on malformed input rather than a clean validation error; not exploitable beyond a minor DoS-by-error-spam or confusing error message, since requireAuth() already gates the endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Change the guard to `if (stageIdx < 0 || stageIdx >= outline.stages.length) return c.json({ error: 'Stage index out of range' }, 400);`

findings.title: ai-curriculum-gen/structure and module-stream routes bypass aiGateway, have no token-usage recording, and no bound on requested module count
findings.detail: Unlike every other curriculum AI route (analyzer, export, builder, incremental — all of which call `recordAiTokenUsage`), routes-ai-curriculum-generator.ts calls the Anthropic API directly via raw `fetch` (lines 340-352, 523-541) and never calls `recordAiTokenUsage`. Additionally, `buildStructurePrompt` (lines 80-92) computes `totalModules` from user-supplied `totalFlightHours / flightLessonDurationMin` etc. with no upper bound check before sending the request — a caller supplying a very small `flightLessonDurationMin` (e.g. 1) with a large `totalFlightHours` can request an enormous number of modules, and since Phase 2 (module-stream) is called once per module from the client in a loop, this multiplies into many uncapped, unmetered Claude API calls.
findings.impact: Token spend for this specific curriculum-generation flow is invisible to whatever admin dashboard/reporting consumes `recordAiTokenUsage` data, undercounting real AI cost. Combined with the missing bound on module count, a malformed or malicious payload (e.g. `flightLessonDurationMin: 1`, `totalFlightHours: 1000`) could trigger thousands of individual Claude calls from the client loop with no server-side cap.
findings.recommendation: Route these calls through `aiGateway` like the sibling routes for consistent metering, add `recordAiTokenUsage` calls using the response's `usage` data, and add a sanity cap on computed `totalModules` (e.g. reject or clamp above ~150) in buildStructurePrompt / the /structure route handler before calling Claude.

findings.title: buildStructurePrompt has no division-by-zero guard on lesson-duration inputs
findings.detail: Lines 81-90: `Math.ceil((answers.totalFlightHours * 60) / answers.flightLessonDurationMin)` and the ground/sim equivalents divide directly by user-supplied `flightLessonDurationMin` / `groundLessonDurationMin` with no check for zero or negative values. If a client sends `0`, the result is `Infinity` or `NaN`, which gets embedded directly into the prompt text sent to Claude (e.g. 'Flight lessons: Infinity × 0 min').
findings.impact: Malformed request produces a nonsensical prompt sent to the paid AI API, wasting a call and likely getting a garbage/error structure response rather than a clean validation rejection.
findings.recommendation: Validate `flightLessonDurationMin`, `groundLessonDurationMin`, `simLessonDurationMin` are positive integers before calling buildStructurePrompt; return 400 otherwise.

findings.title: curriculum-export routes take the full curriculum payload from the request body with no ownership/tenant check
findings.detail: POST /curriculum-export/generate and POST /curriculum-export/revise-page both accept an arbitrary `curriculum`/`module` object directly in the request body (lines 289-302, 566-584) and never look it up by ID against the DB scoped to `orgId` — they only call `requireAuth()` plus a best-effort `resolveOrgIdFromSession` used solely for token-usage attribution, not authorization. Any authenticated user (any org) can submit any curriculum shape they construct client-side and get it converted through Claude into an export document.
findings.impact: Low real-world impact since the caller already possesses/constructs the full curriculum content in the request — no cross-tenant data is exfiltrated that the caller didn't already have. But it does mean these two endpoints provide unmetered/unrestricted AI generation to any authenticated user regardless of which org's curriculum data they submit, and token usage is billed to whatever orgId the caller happens to resolve to rather than being enforced against a curriculum record's actual owning org.
findings.recommendation: If curriculum export is meant to be scoped per-org/per-curriculum-record, look the curriculum up by ID + orgId server-side rather than trusting the client-submitted object wholesale. If the current design (client sends full object) is intentional (e.g. for previewing unsaved edits), document that decision explicitly.

findings.title: buildFallbackSummary / computeHoursFromStages assume duration is a plain number; no defense against non-numeric or negative durations from AI or client
findings.detail: `computeHoursFromStages` (lines 202-237) does `const dur = m.duration ?? 0;` with no `Number()` coercion or NaN/negative guard, unlike the analogous `computeHours` in routes-ai-curriculum-analyzer.ts (line 159: `Number(m.duration) || 0`) and routes-curriculum-export.ts (line 194, same pattern). If the AI-generated JSON ever returns `duration` as a string (e.g. `"60"`) or omits proper numeric typing, `flightMin += dur` will silently produce `NaN` propagating into `summary.hours`, which is displayed to users and used for FAR-compliance pass/fail determination (buildFallbackSummary lines 801-809).
findings.impact: A malformed AI response could silently corrupt the hours summary and FAR-compliance calculation (a domain-critical field for FAA-regulated training) with `NaN`, which downstream UI likely renders as blank or 'NaN' rather than a caught validation error.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same `Number(m.duration) || 0` coercion pattern used in the sibling analyzer/export computeHours functions to computeHoursFromStages for consistency and defensive parsing of AI output.

findings.title: routes-ai-curriculum-builder.ts POST /ai-curriculum/build stores the full request body via `as never` with only 3 fields validated
findings.detail: Line 603-617: the handler validates only `programType`, `regulatoryFramework`, `locationId` are present, then inserts the entire parsed JSON body directly into `curriculumBuildJobs.builderParams` via `body as never` (line 630) — bypassing TypeScript's structural checking entirely. Nested fields like `targetHours.total/dual/solo/sim/ground`, `stageCount`, `contentCustomization`, etc. are never validated for type or range (e.g. `stageCount` could be `0`, negative, or a string; `targetHours` could be missing entirely, which would then produce `NaN`/`undefined` deep inside `buildCurriculumPrompt`, e.g. line 479's template interpolation).
findings.impact: A malformed request that passes the 3-field check but has garbage/missing nested fields still enqueues a DB row and an Inngest job, wasting a build slot and a Claude API call before failing deep inside prompt construction or parsing — rather than being rejected cleanly at the API boundary.
findings.recommendation: Add a zod (or similar) schema validating BuilderParams shape (or at minimum stageCount > 0 and targetHours.* are positive numbers) before the DB insert, matching the level of validation the analyzer/export routes apply to their inputs (title/stages presence checks).

result.note: Verified both routes in routes-micamp.ts. Void (L595-660) and refund (L662-738) both load the transaction via db.query.paymentTransactions.findFirst({ where: eq(schema.paymentTransactions.id, txId) }) — no flightSchoolId scoping to the caller's school (L602-604, L671-673). Refund path (L703) only checks partialAmount >= transaction.amount against the single request; it never sums prior 'refund' rows for the same original transaction, so repeated sub-threshold partial refunds can exceed the original charge, each triggering a live loaded.client.refund() call to MiCamp. Severity HIGH is correct as stated.

Verified against src/lib/micamp.ts L57-105: authenticate() reads this.bearerToken/this.tokenExpiresAt, awaits fetch on cache-miss, then writes the token — a genuine TOCTOU race if this client instance is ever shared across concurrent callers. Finding accurately describes the code and explicitly concedes it's not an active bug today (fresh client constructed per request). Given it's a latent/hypothetical issue with no current exploitable path, MEDIUM reads a bit high — LOW is more accurate (finder itself marked confidence: low). Recommendation (in-flight promise guard, or drop the misleading cache fields until actually needed) is sound and cheap to apply preemptively.

Verified against routes-micamp.ts L595-738 and micamp.ts L107-184: void (L625-633) and refund (L697-707) both call MiCamp's live API before the DB status update, with no compensation/wrapping if the DB write fails or the process crashes between steps. The guard at L610/L679 checks the same stale local status field that the post-call update writes, so a client retry after partial failure would re-trigger the MiCamp call. Confirmed voidTransaction/refund request bodies (L154-184 in micamp.ts) contain no client-generated idempotency/reference key — MiCamp has no server-side way to dedupe a retried request. Severity HIGH is correct given this is unrecoverable money-movement drift with no reconciliation mechanism.

findings.title: Standby-aircraft routes never verify :locationId belongs to the caller's org (cross-tenant write/read)
findings.detail: All 6 routes in this file (lines 274, 451, 492, 555, 608, 752) call `resolveOrgIdFromSession(authUser)` WITHOUT passing the Hono context `c`. This resolves `orgId` purely from the caller's own email/membership and never uses `:locationId` from the URL at all. Compare to the sibling file `routes-standby.ts`, which correctly calls `resolveOrgIdFromSession(authUser, c)` (with `c`) in every route — the `c` parameter is what lets `resolveOrgIdFromSession` (helpers.ts:325-339) derive/validate org from the location for super-admins, and more importantly there is NO other check anywhere in routes-standby-aircraft.ts that `locationId` belongs to `orgId`. A regular authenticated user from Org A can POST `/locations/{orgB-locationId}/schedule/standby-aircraft` and the row is written with their own `orgId` but an arbitrary `locationId` belonging to another school. Additionally, the activation conflict-check at line 628 calls `scheduleRepository.findByLocationAndDate(locationId, ...)`, which filters only by `locationId` with no `flightSchoolId` predicate (repository impl line 3780), so activation can read/report conflicts against another org's real schedule events.
findings.impact: A non-admin user can create, list, activate, or dismiss standby schedule events tied to another flight school's location — polluting another org's schedule and leaking scheduling data (student/instructor names, times) cross-tenant via the conflict-check response.
findings.recommendation: Pass `c` to `resolveOrgIdFromSession(authUser, c)` in every route in this file (matching routes-standby.ts), and additionally verify `locationId` resolves to the caller's `orgId` via `mvpRepository.locations.findFlightSchoolIdByLocation` (the same pattern used correctly in routes-aircraft-vor-log.ts's `ensureLocationAndAircraftAccess`). Also add `flightSchoolId`/orgId scoping to `findByLocationAndDate` in mvp-v2.repository.impl.ts.

findings.title: Fail-open tenant check in aircraft logbook routes when org resolution returns null
findings.detail: Two tenant guards fail OPEN instead of closed: (1) line 119 `verifyLogbookTenant`: `if (userOrgId && lb.flightSchoolId !== userOrgId) throw new Error('FORBIDDEN')` — when `userOrgId` is null/falsy, the whole condition short-circuits false and the check is skipped entirely. (2) line 174 in the `/aircraft-logbook/:equipmentId/logbooks` handler: `if (userOrgId && aircraft.flightSchoolId !== userOrgId) return 403` — same pattern. `resolveOrgIdFromSession` → `resolveOrgIdFromEmail` (helpers.ts:275-305) legitimately returns `null` whenever an authenticated user's email doesn't resolve to a row in `users` or `team_members` (e.g. deactivated account, onboarding race, data drift) — this is a real, reachable state, not merely theoretical.
findings.impact: An authenticated user whose session doesn't resolve to any org membership can view/modify ANY flight school's aircraft maintenance logbooks, entries, and amendments (FAA Part 43 compliance records) — since both guards silently let the request through when `userOrgId` is null instead of denying it.
findings.recommendation: Invert both checks to fail closed: `if (!userOrgId || lb.flightSchoolId !== userOrgId) throw/return 403`. Apply the same fix pattern anywhere else `if (userOrgId && ...)` is used as a tenant gate.

findings.title: Parts stock quantity race condition — read-then-write with no transaction or row lock
findings.detail: `POST /parts/:id/transactions` (lines 594-694) reads the current `part` (qtyOnHand/qtyReserved), validates `part.qtyOnHand + signedQty >= 0` in application code, inserts a transaction row, then does a separate `UPDATE partsCatalog SET qtyOnHand = ...` using the value computed from the earlier read — all as unguarded, non-atomic, non-transactional statements (no `db.transaction()`, no `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, no atomic `qtyOnHand = qtyOnHand + $delta` SQL expression).
findings.impact: Two concurrent transactions against the same part (e.g. two mechanics scanning the same part on different work orders within the same second) can both read the same `qtyOnHand`, both pass the negative-stock check independently, and both write — one overwriting the other's update. This can drive `qtyOnHand` negative in the DB despite the application-level guard, or silently lose one of the two transactions' quantity effect while still recording both transaction ledger rows (so the ledger and the catalog quantity diverge).
findings.recommendation: Wrap the read-check-insert-update sequence in a DB transaction, and update `qtyOnHand`/`qtyReserved` using an atomic SQL expression (`SET qty_on_hand = qty_on_hand + ${signedQty}`) with a `WHERE qty_on_hand + ${signedQty} >= 0` guard so the negative-stock check is enforced atomically by the database rather than by a stale application-level read.

findings.title: Part status 'expired' is dead code — branch order bug hides expired shelf-life parts as 'expiring_soon'
findings.detail: `deriveStatus()` (lines 58-77) checks `if (daysUntilExpiry <= 30) return 'expiring_soon';` BEFORE `if (daysUntilExpiry < 0) return 'expired';`. Since any negative number is also `<= 30`, the expired branch can never be reached — an already-expired part is always classified as 'expiring_soon'. The frontend (`part-detail.tsx` PartStatus type, `parts-scanner.tsx` STATUS_CFG) fully defines and displays a distinct 'expired' status (red, distinguishable from amber 'expiring_soon'), but the backend can never emit it. The GET /parts summary object (lines 147-153) also omits an `expired` count entirely, consistent with this dead branch.
findings.impact: Shelf-life-expired parts (which may be unusable/unairworthy per aviation parts traceability requirements) are visually indistinguishable from parts merely approaching expiry, understating urgency to mechanics/inventory staff reviewing the parts list.
findings.recommendation: Swap the branch order: check `daysUntilExpiry < 0` (expired) before `daysUntilExpiry <= 30` (expiring_soon). Also add an `expired` key to the GET /parts summary aggregation to match the frontend's PartsSummary expectations used elsewhere (parts-scanner.tsx already expects `summary.expired`).

findings.title: Equipment profile edit applies optimistic local state update with no rollback on save failure
findings.detail: `handleSaveEdit` (lines 1004-1076) calls `setEq(updated)` at line 1068 BEFORE `await persistEquipmentUpdate(updated)` at line 1069. If the PUT request fails, the catch block (lines 1072-1074) only shows an error toast — it never reverts `eq` back to the pre-edit server state.
findings.impact: After a failed save, the UI continues to display the user's unsaved edits (weight & balance figures, TBO hours, status, etc.) as if they succeeded, even though the server still holds the old values. A page refresh or navigation away/back silently reverts to the real (older) data, which will read as data loss/corruption to the user who believed the save succeeded from the UI's own display.
findings.recommendation: Capture the pre-edit `eq` value, and in the catch block call `setEq(previousEq)` to roll back the optimistic update on failure — or defer `setEq(updated)` until after `persistEquipmentUpdate` resolves successfully.

findings.title: Standby-queue cancel button has no error handling — silent failure on delete
findings.detail: `handleCancel` (lines 144-150) does `await fetch(...DELETE...)` with no `res.ok` check and no try/catch. If the DELETE request fails (network error, 404, 500), the fetch promise rejects unhandled (React logs an unhandled rejection) or resolves with a non-2xx status that is never inspected, and `fetchEntries()` is still called (refetching unchanged data) with zero user-facing feedback. This matches the project's own documented anti-pattern in CLAUDE.md ('Silent Catch Blocks Prohibited' — user sees no error indication).
findings.impact: A student clicking 'Cancel' on a standby request that fails server-side sees the entry silently remain in their list (or briefly disappear from optimistic UI expectations then return) with no error toast/message explaining why, leading to confusion or duplicate cancel attempts.
findings.recommendation: Wrap in try/catch, check `res.ok`, and surface a toast/error message on failure (mirroring the pattern already used correctly in `handleAdd` in the same file, and in the parallel `StudentStandbyPanel.handleLeave` implementation).

findings.title: PATCH /parts/:id allows duplicate partNumber with no uniqueness check
findings.detail: `PATCH /parts/:id` (lines 344-424) allows updating `partNumber` (line 383-384) with no check against existing parts in the same org/location for a duplicate part number, unlike `routes-aircraft-make-models.ts` which explicitly catches and translates a unique-constraint violation (`aircraft_make_models_unique_idx`) into a friendly 409. If there's no DB-level unique constraint on `(flightSchoolId, partNumber)` either, two catalog rows can end up with the same part number.
findings.impact: Duplicate part numbers in the same school's catalog would break part lookup/scan flows (`parts-scanner.tsx` ManualLookup search, QR scan resolution) — ambiguous which catalog row a physical part maps to, and could cause the wrong part's stock to be decremented on a work-order scan.
findings.recommendation: Add a unique index on `(flight_school_id, part_number)` (or location-scoped equivalent) in the schema, and catch/translate the constraint violation in both POST and PATCH handlers the same way aircraft-make-models.ts does.

findings.title: Two parallel, inconsistent standby-request implementations for students
findings.detail: `student-standby.tsx` (page at presumably /standby) talks directly to `/locations/:locationId/schedule/standby` (backed by `routes-standby.ts` / `scheduleStandbyRepository`, a separate 'notify first-in-queue' waitlist keyed by date/time slot). `student-standby-panel.tsx` (a drawer component) talks to a completely different service (`../services/standby` — `fetchStandbyOpportunities`/`joinStandby`/`leaveStandby`), which appears to target actual `scheduleEvents` rows with an `approvalStatus` field (`auto_approved`/`pending_review`/`rejected`) — a different data model than `StandbyEntry` in the page file (`status: waiting/notified/confirmed/expired/cancelled`). These look like two independently built standby subsystems with different backing tables/statuses, not a shared component reused across two entry points.
findings.impact: Feature drift risk — a student using one entry point (drawer vs. full page) sees different standby state/behavior than the other; future bug fixes applied to one implementation won't propagate to the other, and it's unclear from the code which is the current source of truth.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with product/architecture whether both standby systems are intentionally distinct (e.g. one for schedule-event-based standby, one for date/time-slot waitlist) — if not, consolidate onto one data model and one set of routes.

result.note: Verified against actual code. L477 Math.round(amount * feePercent/100) correctly yields integer cents. L481 totalCharged/100 = amountDollars is unnormalized float division, flows into invoiceData.TotalAmount (L485) and client.saleWithToken(amountDollars,...) (L504) with no .toFixed()/rounding guard. Same pattern at L695 refundAmountCents/100 -> L699 loaded.client.refund(...). Checked src/lib/micamp.ts downstream: amountDollars is passed straight through as Amount/TotalAmount in all three request bodies (Sale L118, saleWithToken L143, Refund L180) with zero normalization anywhere in the call chain — so the recommended fix (Number((cents/100).toFixed(2)) applied both at the callers and centrally in micamp.ts) is correctly scoped. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: affects only a subset of cent values (documented IEEE-754 non-round-trip cases), and JSON serialization + a competent gateway JSON parser will often coerce correctly, but this is live payment-gateway money math with no compensating guard, so MEDIUM (not LOW) stands; no evidence of actual incidents to justify HIGH/CRITICAL.

Verified against src/server/routes/routes-micamp.ts lines 771-811. Two unpaginated full-table scans (flightSchools, paymentProcessorConfigs filtered by processor) joined in-memory via a Map, no limit/offset. merchantKey and processingFeePercent are returned per school. Endpoint is gated by requireSuperAdmin(), consistent with the finding's low-severity framing (internal admin tool, not a public/tenant-facing endpoint). Severity LOW is appropriate as given — a genuine but low-urgency scalability smell, not a correctness or security bug.

Verified at src/server/routes/routes-micamp.ts:318-321. No regex/format validation on expirationDate, no bounds check on month (1-12), no expiry-in-past check, Number.parseInt on malformed input produces NaN. Schema confirmed (src/lib/schema/index.ts:7010-7011): studentPaymentMethods.expMonth/expYear are integer().notNull() — a NaN insert will fail at the DB layer, surfacing as an opaque 502 rather than a clean 400, matching the finding's stated impact. Century-rollover claim (hardcoded '20' prefix) is real but cosmetic (only breaks post-2099); the load-bearing defect is the missing input validation. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: billing-adjacent path (MiCamp card tokenization) but the failure mode is a bad UX/error-clarity issue, not a security or data-integrity breach. Recommendation (regex MM/YY check, month 1-12, not-in-past, return 400) is correct and actionable.

Verified against actual code. schema/index.ts L7017-7019 defines uniqueIndex('spm_student_school_processor_uniq') on (studentId, flightSchoolId, processor) exactly as claimed. routes-micamp.ts L323-337 POST /micamp/cards does a plain db.insert(schema.studentPaymentMethods).values(...).returning() with no onConflictDoUpdate. Generic catch at L349-353 returns 502 with e.message on any error, including a Postgres unique-violation on re-insert. Contrast with /micamp/connect (L136-171) which does use onConflictDoUpdate on the analogous unique(flightSchoolId, processor) constraint — confirms the asymmetric pattern the finding describes. No call to deleteToken() anywhere in the POST /micamp/cards handler, so a prior token is never revoked. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: real data-integrity/orphaned-resource + confusing-error bug, not a security vuln or data-loss bug; requires student to already have a card on file to trigger.

Verified at src/server/routes/routes-micamp.ts L484: InvoiceNumber falls back to `pay-${Date.now()}` (ms resolution) when invoiceId is absent. Verified L503-507 (saleWithToken call) and surrounding handler: no idempotency key/token is passed to MiCamp, and no pre-check against existing paymentTransactions rows occurs before charging — a client retry (timeout, double-click) would produce a genuinely new charge with no server-side dedup. Endpoint is requireAuth() only, no debounce/rate-limit visible. This file is in the billing-protected surface (docs/billing/protected-paths.txt likely applies) so any fix requires BILLING-APPROVED:<id> per CLAUDE.md. Severity LOW is appropriate — real latent risk requiring specific timing to trigger, not an observed/active incident.

Verified against src/lib/micamp.ts lines 264-301. response.json() at L282 has no dedicated try/catch; on a non-JSON body (HTML error page, empty body, proxy timeout page) it throws SyntaxError, caught only by the outer catch (L296-300) and surfaced as a generic 'Transaction error: SyntaxError...' — indistinguishable from a genuine decline message. Severity LOW is correct: functionally the error still propagates/is caught (no crash, no silent failure), it's purely an observability/on-call-debugging gap.

Verified both matchInvoiceToExisting (lines 1845-1871) and matchPaymentToExisting (1873-1898) in src/server/stripe/school-stripe-service.ts. Neither call uses .returning(), and both do `return updated !== null` where `updated` is the resolved query-result object from Drizzle's neon-serverless update() — never null. The WHERE clause includes isNull(stripeInvoiceId)/isNull(stripePaymentIntentId) guards, so a stale matchId or an already-matched record causes a silent zero-row no-op that still returns true. Severity HIGH is appropriate given this is billing-adjacent (Stripe reconciliation) and produces silent ledger drift with no error surfaced to the admin.

Verified lines 170-207 of src/app/api/stripe-webhook/route.ts. The typeof-check branch is real; production NeonDatabase always has onConflictDoNothing so the fallback (findExistingStripeWebhookReceipt then bare insert, no transaction) is dead code in prod and a genuine TOCTOU race only reachable via a mock db lacking the method. Severity LOW is correctly assigned given zero production reachability.

Verified directly in drizzle/meta/_journal.json (lines 621-641): idx 89 has tag \"0091_add_workflow_canvas_fields\" (when: 1774950000000) and idx 91 has tag \"0089_add_stage_check_tables\" (when: 1774810000000) — confirmed swapped, with idx 90 correctly sandwiched between them as \"0090_add_announcements\". Both referenced SQL files (drizzle/0089_add_stage_check_tables.sql, drizzle/0091_add_workflow_canvas_fields.sql) exist on disk under their filename-prefix-matching names, so the mismatch is isolated to the journal idx field, not the files themselves. Confirmed .husky/pre-push has orphan-file, orphan-snapshot, and cross-branch idx-conflict checks (grep for jq entries[].idx logic) but no check comparing entry.idx to its own tag's numeric filename prefix — grepping the hook for split/parseInt/prefix-match patterns returns nothing. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate as stated: real integrity/tooling gap with correctly-assessed low current blast radius (both entries already applied everywhere per the finding's cited repair history) but a genuine landmine for future debugging.

findings.title: PUT /checkride-history/:id lets any authenticated user directly set feeBilled and invoiceId, bypassing the actual billing flow
findings.detail: The general-purpose checkride history update route (PUT /locations/:locationId/checkride-history/:id) is gated only by requireAuth() (any authenticated school user, not requireAdmin()). Its zod schema (checkrideHistoryUpdateSchema, lines 146-148) accepts examinerFee, feeBilled, and invoiceId directly in the body, and the handler writes them verbatim to the DB (lines 2321-2329) with no validation that an actual invoice with that id exists, that the fee was computed correctly, or that any of the dedicated billing logic (createCheckrideInvoice, settleInvoiceByPaymentPreference, audit logging) ran. This sits alongside three purpose-built endpoints (/bill, /student-signoff, /override-signoff) that DO perform real invoice creation, payment settlement, and audit trail — but this generic PUT lets any of those safeguards be skipped entirely. The frontend (checkride-queue.tsx saveExaminerFee) only ever sends {examinerFee}, confirming feeBilled/invoiceId via PUT is unused-but-reachable surface, not a deliberate feature.
findings.impact: Any authenticated non-admin user at the school (e.g., an instructor account) could mark a checkride fee as 'billed' with a fabricated invoiceId without any invoice or payment ever being created, hiding an unpaid fee from the Billing Queue (pending-signoff/unbilled lists filter on feeBilled=false) — or conversely, corrupt a real billed record by resetting examinerFee/feeBilled, breaking the record's audit trail and student balance.
findings.recommendation: Remove examinerFee/feeBilled/invoiceId from the general PUT schema (or require requireAdmin() plus dedicated validation matching the /bill flow), and route all fee-state transitions exclusively through /bill, /student-signoff, and /override-signoff.

findings.title: TOCTOU race allows double-billing a checkride examiner fee (duplicate invoices)
findings.detail: All three billing-mutation endpoints (POST /bill, POST /student-signoff, POST /override-signoff) follow the same pattern: SELECT the checkrideHistory row, check `record.feeBilled` in application code, then later run createCheckrideInvoice() followed by an UPDATE that sets feeBilled=true. The UPDATE is not conditioned on `feeBilled = false` (no `WHERE feeBilled = false` guard, no transaction wrapping the check-then-act), and there is no unique DB constraint tying checkrideHistoryId to at most one invoice (confirmed via grep of schema/index.ts — no unique index on studentInvoices for checkrideHistoryId). Two concurrent requests (double-click, or a student sign-off racing an admin override) can both read feeBilled=false before either write lands.
findings.impact: Duplicate invoices/charges for the same checkride examiner fee, incorrectly reducing the student's account balance twice and creating a billing reconciliation problem.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the check-then-act in a single transaction with `UPDATE ... SET feeBilled=true WHERE id=$1 AND feeBilled=false RETURNING *` and only proceed to invoice creation if a row was returned (or create the invoice first inside the transaction and roll back on conflict). Alternatively add a partial unique index on studentInvoices(checkrideHistoryId) WHERE type='checkride_fee'.

findings.title: GET checkride-history list exposes all students' checkride results and billing data to any authenticated school user with no role/ownership filter
findings.detail: GET /locations/:locationId/checkride-history is gated only by requireAuth() with a location-ownership (tenant) check, but no per-user/per-role filtering. It returns the entire school's checkride history including every student's name, examiner fee, feeBilled/invoiceId status, disapproval areas, and instructor names. Unlike the training-certificate-ratings routes and several checkride admin actions in this same file which correctly gate mutation on requireAdmin()/isTenantAdmin(), this read endpoint has no equivalent restriction — any authenticated principal for the tenant (which could include a student-role account, depending on how student sessions are issued elsewhere in the app) can enumerate every other student's checkride outcomes and fees.
findings.impact: Cross-student PII and financial data exposure within a single school if student accounts share the same requireAuth() session/role surface used elsewhere (e.g., stage-check schedule endpoints are explicitly commented as tenant-scoped only, implying students CAN authenticate against these Hono routes).
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether student role accounts can reach this route; if so, add a role check (staff/admin-only) or filter results to the caller's own studentId when the caller's role is 'student'.

findings.title: Lead-bonus PATCH allows any authenticated user to self-verify their own instructor bonus with no admin gate
findings.detail: PATCH /locations/:locationId/checkride-history/:checkrideId/lead-bonus is gated only by requireAuth() and lets the caller set leadInstructorId, onTime, firstPass, and verified directly. Nothing checks that the caller is an admin, or that the caller is not the leadInstructorId being verified. This contrasts with the rest of the file's careful isTenantAdmin()/requireAdmin() gating on financially meaningful fields (examiner email, packet template admin actions, etc.).
findings.impact: An instructor could set their own lead-bonus record's verified: true (self-attesting eligibility for a bonus) without any admin review, if the UI surfaces this control to non-admin instructor accounts. No downstream payroll automation was found consuming this field in the current codebase, which limits the immediate blast radius, but the field's name and shape strongly suggest compensation intent.
findings.recommendation: Gate `verified` (and ideally the whole endpoint) behind requireAdmin(), or at minimum reject a request where the acting user's id equals leadInstructorId.

findings.title: Stage-check schedule PUT does not verify cross-school ownership of checkInstructorId/aircraftId being reassigned
findings.detail: PUT /stage-checks/schedules/:id updates checkInstructorId and aircraftId when they pass isUuid(), but unlike the POST handler (which calls studentBelongsToOrg before insert), the PUT path never verifies the new checkInstructorId or aircraftId belongs to the same flightSchoolId. Only their UUID shape is checked.
findings.impact: A caller could reassign a stage-check schedule to an instructor id or aircraft id belonging to a different school (a dangling/foreign reference), though this doesn't leak data cross-tenant since the row itself remains scoped — it's a referential-integrity gap rather than an access-control bypass.
findings.recommendation: Add the same org-ownership check used in the POST handler (a small userBelongsToOrg/aircraftBelongsToOrg helper) before accepting checkInstructorId/aircraftId updates.

findings.title: Stage-check area results insert has no server-side validation on result/code values
findings.detail: POST /stage-checks/results inserts body.areaResults directly into stageCheckAreaResults with no validation that result is one of an allowed enum (e.g. pass/fail) or that acsAreaCode/acsAreaName are non-empty, unlike the checkride outcome area schema in routes-checkrides.ts (checkrideOutcomeAreaSchema) which uses zod with length limits.
findings.impact: Malformed or empty ACS area result rows can be persisted, and the remediation-trigger logic elsewhere (fireStageCheckTrigger, which filters ar.result === 'fail') will silently miss malformed results that don't exactly match the expected string.
findings.recommendation: Add a zod schema for areaResults mirroring checkrideOutcomeAreaSchema, validating result against an explicit enum.

result.notes: Enumerated all owned files: routes-checkrides.ts (5839 lines, all sections read), routes-stage-checks.ts (1430 lines, full), routes-training-certificate-ratings.ts (1077 lines, full), src/lib/checkride/generate-packet-pdf.ts (full, client-side PDF composition, no security surface), checkride-completion-event-type.ts, checkride-completion-scheduling.ts, checkride-outcome-document-upload.ts, checkride-standards.ts (static FAA seed data, low risk), training-certificate-ratings.ts (full). checkride-queue.tsx (7499 lines) was spot-checked via targeted grep + read around fee/billing/date logic given its size and that it is a thin client over the already-reviewed backend routes; the two client calls inspected (saveExaminerFee, billFeeToStudent) corroborate the PUT-bypass finding rather than introduce new independent bugs. The file overall shows strong existing security hardening (many comments reference TD-7 IDOR fixes), so most remaining risk is concentrated in billing-adjacent race conditions and role-gating gaps rather than basic tenant-isolation holes. This file is billing-adjacent but not listed in docs/billing/protected-paths.txt, so findings were reported per the read-only scan mandate without any code modification.

result.note: Verified against actual code. package.json:11 confirms generate-migration-manifest.js is wired only to `prebuild` (runs during `npm run build`), not pre-push or CI. .husky/pre-push does schema-drift/journal-integrity checks but never touches migration-manifest.ts. db-health.ts:21 does exact `appliedCount !== MIGRATION_COUNT` and fires Sentry.captureMessage(..., 'error') on any mismatch. Drift is not hypothetical: drizzle/meta/_journal.json currently has 418 entries with latest tag '0426_register_atp_frc_analytics_v2_flags', while the committed manifest (src/generated/migration-manifest.ts) says MIGRATION_COUNT=416 / LATEST_MIGRATION='0424_rate_null_subject_uniqueness' — a live, present-tense false-positive condition feeding production Sentry alerts right now. Severity HIGH is appropriate: active alert-fatigue/false-signal defect on an ops monitoring surface, not data loss or outage (so not CRITICAL).

Verified against src/app/api/stripe-webhook/route.ts lines 1291-1320. handleCustomerUpdated reads customer.email, compares case-insensitively to the matched user's current email (line 1310), and on mismatch writes it directly (1312-1315) with only a console.log (1317-1319) — no auditLogs insert. Confirmed 8 other handlers in the same file (lines 497, 540, 744, 816, 854, 952, 1036, 1080) do write to schema.auditLogs, so this handler is a genuine outlier from the file's own established pattern. No validation or confirmation step gates the write. Severity MEDIUM is reasonable: email is auth/notification-adjacent and the trust boundary crossed (Stripe Connect-side data → ATOS user record) is real, but exploitation requires an actor with access to edit the customer object on that school's Stripe Connect account, so it is not broadly/remotely exploitable and causes no data loss — MEDIUM fits better than HIGH.

Verified against src/app/api/stripe-webhook/route.ts. Lines 909-912: piPaymentMethod ternary — both branches return null, so it's provably always null. Line 942: void piPaymentMethod suppresses the unused-var lint on this dead value. Line 916: dynamic `const { stripeClient } = await import('@/lib/stripe')` inside handleDisputeCreated, despite `stripeClient` already imported at module scope on line 15 and used elsewhere in the file. No functional impact — the real PM-block logic runs via the charge lookup (lines 914-941) using the locally-shadowed dynamic import, which works correctly, just redundantly. Severity LOW is correct: pure dead-code/maintenance-trap issue, no behavior change on fix (delete lines 909-912 and 942, replace dynamic import with the module-scope stripeClient reference).

Verified against scripts/db-migrate.ts (2,425 lines, confirmed via wc -l). Contains dozens of hardcoded tag-specific repair functions/blocks (0021, 0035/0039, 0061, 0064/0083, 0069, 0075/0174, 0078/0082, 0079/0080, 0099/0100, 0132/0133/0141, 0221/0223/0227, 0296, 0315, etc.), each heavily narrative-commented (284+ comment/postmortem lines) citing specific production incidents, each gated on an existence/tracked check before running idempotent DDL (e.g. repairWorkOrderSoftDeleteMigration at line 82 checks journal entry, hash, table existence, then tracked status before doing anything) — so no active bug today, matches the finding's own characterization. runMigrations() (line 2372) calls repairMissingTrackingRows() and applyTimestampSkippedMigrations() unconditionally on every run, THEN checks areAllMigrationsTracked() (line 2405) only to decide whether to skip Drizzle's migrate() call — the probes/repairs themselves are never short-circuited even when the DB is fully tracked. This confirms the recommendation (short-circuit probes once areAllMigrationsTracked() is true) is a real, unimplemented optimization, not already done. Severity LOW is correct — maintainability/query-overhead concern, not a functional defect.

Verified in src/lib/db.ts and src/lib/db-tenant-context.ts. db is a Proxy over a shared @neondatabase/serverless Pool (max 8, db.ts:31-36); getDb()/drizzle(pool) exposes db.execute() which checks out an arbitrary pooled connection per call. setTenantContext (db-tenant-context.ts:11-21) issues two separate db.execute() calls with set_config(..., is_local=true) and never uses db.transaction() or pool.connect() to pin a client, so both the pairing of the two set_config calls and any subsequent tenant query are not guaranteed to land on the same physical connection. Postgres set_config with is_local=true is transaction-scoped and reverts per-connection, so the finding's mechanism (context set on one connection, next query serviced by a different pooled connection with stale or no context) is accurate. Severity HIGH is correct.

Verified against src/lib/idempotency.ts lines 9-42. Check (SELECT, lines 15-19) and act (handler + INSERT, lines 31-38) are not wrapped in a transaction and there's no SELECT...FOR UPDATE or advisory lock. Two concurrent calls with the same key both pass the empty-SELECT check, both execute handler(), and only the INSERT winner's row persists (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING silently drops the loser's insert) — the loser still returns cached:false with its own executed-but-discarded result. Matches finding precisely. Severity MEDIUM is reasonable: real correctness bug in the utility itself, but finding correctly notes no production callers currently exist, so actual impact is latent.

Verified both implementations exist as described with matching line numbers. routes-stripe.ts findCandidateCustomers (244-324) has confidence scoring, phone matching, failOnSearchError; school-stripe-service.ts findCustomerCandidates (449-508) lacks all three and returns raw unsorted Stripe.Customer[]. Additional finding: findCustomerCandidates has ZERO external callers (grep confirms only its interface declaration at line 59 and class definition at 449 — no call sites anywhere in src/). It is dead code, which makes the recommendation's second option (remove the unused method) the more accurate fix rather than consolidation. Severity LOW is correct given it's unreachable code, not actively duplicated business logic.

Verified: package.json:42 defines check:tenant-guard → tsx scripts/check-tenant-write-guard.ts. Read full .husky/pre-push (354 lines) — its 4 documented responsibilities are schema drift, journal integrity, tsc typecheck, and Neon teardown; no reference to check:tenant-guard or check-tenant-write-guard anywhere. Grepped all 28 files in .github/workflows/*.yml — zero matches for either string. Script header (lines 1-23) confirms it guards two specific prior-incident regression classes (F2 derive-from-URL missing org guard, F1/F4 hardcoded PII roster) via git ls-files-based static analysis, exit 1 on violation. The gate is real and functional but completely unwired from any enforcement point — finding is accurate as stated. HIGH is justified: it's a multi-tenant-isolation/security guard with cited prior production incidents, not a cosmetic or nit-tier gap.

Fully verified against actual code. src/lib/db-tenant-context.ts defines setTenantContext()/clearTenantContext() (calling set_config('app.flight_school_id', ...) and set_config('app.is_superadmin', ...)) but a repo-wide grep confirms zero callers anywhere else in src/ — no middleware, no route wires these in. drizzle/0144_enable_row_level_security.sql confirmed: loops over ~80 tenant-scoped tables, runs ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus tenant_isolation (SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE) and tenant_insert (INSERT) policies, both gated on get_current_flight_school_id() which reads current_setting('app.flight_school_id', true). Since nothing ever calls set_config, that GUC is always unset -> get_current_flight_school_id() returns NULL and is_superadmin() defaults false, so in practice RLS policies evaluate false for every row on every RLS-enabled table (a hard-fail/all-rows-hidden posture) rather than a pure pass-through no-op — a nuance worth noting, but it doesn't weaken the core finding: the DB-level tenant backstop asserted by the migration/docstrings is not wired into any request path, and app-code WHERE-clause bugs (as seen in routes-stripe.ts's manual scoping pattern) have no RLS backstop today. Severity CRITICAL is appropriate given ADR-002 multi-tenant isolation is a named protected architecture concern and this spans ~80 tables of aviation training/PII data.

Verified directly against code. drizzle/0142: idempotency_keys PK is `key` varchar(255) alone, no tenant/flight_school_id column. src/lib/idempotency.ts:16-18 SELECT and :36-38 INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) both key purely off the caller-supplied `key` string, no tenant qualifier anywhere. Grep confirms zero callers of withIdempotency() outside its own definition — matches the finding's 'landmine dead code, not yet exploitable' framing exactly. Comparison table accounting_provider_idempotency_keys (drizzle/0346) verified: correctly scopes via UNIQUE INDEX on (owner_type, owner_id, provider, provider_account_id, idempotency_key), confirming the recommended pattern exists elsewhere in the codebase. Severity MEDIUM is reasonable — not yet exploitable (no callers) but a real design gap in a primitive likely to be reused for genuine idempotency needs (payments/webhooks) where cross-tenant collision would become live.

Verified against src/lib/db-health.ts lines 13-44. Both swallow points (25-29, 34-38) exist exactly as described; production failure path returns silently at line 39 with no distinguishing signal from a clean pass. Severity LOW confirmed correct — observability-only path, no data-integrity or auth impact.

The narrow technical claim is correct: notDeleted()/liveAnd() in src/server/db/soft-delete.ts have zero callers outside the definition file and its test (verified via grep). However the finding's severity and impact analysis rest on a false premise — it states the required read-filter 'is not applied anywhere in application code' and that 'archived/soft-deleted rows can surface in live queries and the UI.' That is false: a repo-wide grep found 100+ call sites across src/server/api/v1/routes/*, src/server/routes/*, src/repositories/mvp-v2.repository.impl.ts, and src/lib/archive/* that already apply isNull(<table>.deletedAt) filtering directly (the inline primitive) rather than through the unused wrapper helpers. Soft-delete filtering is applied broadly and consistently — the codebase just never adopted the shared helper abstraction. This is dead/unused utility code (worth removing or wiring up for DRY/consistency), not an active data-isolation or archive-integrity gap. Downgrade HIGH to LOW: correct the finding's title/impact before it goes into any client-facing debt register — as written it materially overstates risk (implies archived rows leak into the UI, which is not happening).

Verified src/lib/quickbooks-sync.ts:412 — buildQBUrl(null, updatedMeta) should be buildQBUrl(invoice.invoiceUrl, updatedMeta). buildQBUrl (lines 77-83) only preserves the pre-existing URL prefix when existingUrl is truthy; passing null always produces the bare 'qb:{json}' blob, wiping any prior Stripe/other URL content on every payment sync. invoice.invoiceUrl is already in scope (used at line 362 to parse meta), so this is an unambiguous bug, not intentional. Severity HIGH is appropriate: silent, permanent data loss on a recurring code path with no test coverage evident.

Read src/lib/db-startup-probe.ts in full. Finding is accurate: runSchemaDriftProbe() (line 114) uses its own unpooled new Pool({connectionString: url}) (line 154), diffs information_schema.columns vs the Drizzle schema, and directly executes CREATE TYPE / ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE (ensureEnumType, lines 72-80) and ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS (line 188) against the live DB on every cold start until success — entirely outside drizzle/*.sql + _journal.json, contradicting the PDD-008 rationale. Only console.log/console.error on apply, no alerting/circuit-breaker. Severity MEDIUM confirmed as appropriate: mutation is ADD-only (never drops/renames per code comments), idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS), and the whole operation is wrapped in try/catch so failures fail safe rather than crashing startup — so not HIGH; but it is a real, silent, non-journaled schema-mutation path that PDD-008's migration/journal check has no visibility into, so not LOW either.

Verified exactly as described. src/lib/quickbooks.ts:344 uses name.replace(/'/g, "\\'") (backslash-escape) before embedding into `SELECT * FROM Customer WHERE DisplayName = '${escaped}'` at line 345. QBO's query language uses SQL-style doubled-quote escaping, not backslash-escaping, so this produces a malformed query for any name containing an apostrophe. Confirmed sibling correct implementation at src/server/assistant/tools/native/qbo.ts:140 uses escapeQboString (doubles the quote) for the identical query pattern at line 141, proving the codebase's own established correct convention. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: real customer-facing names with apostrophes (e.g. "O'Brien Aviation") will break findOrCreateQBCustomer and invoice sync, but it's a narrow input-triggered correctness bug, not a security/data-loss issue.

Verified via ls: src/app/api/quickbooks-callback does not exist anywhere in the repo. Confirmed actual paths exist instead: src/app/api/integrations/qbo/callback/route.ts and src/components/features/mvp-v2/pages/quickbooks-callback.tsx. This is a scan-config scope-note issue, not a code defect — severity LOW is appropriate as stated.

Verified against routes-auth.ts:879-939. /delete-user has zero tenant-scoping check (no resolveSameOrgAuthUser call), only requireAdmin() role gate. Directly contrasted by the sibling /update-user-metadata handler (lines 1040-1059 in the same file) which explicitly calls resolveSameOrgAuthUser and returns 403 on cross-org access before writing. resolvedUserId in /delete-user is derived purely from caller input (email lookup or raw userId) and passed straight to auth.api.removeUser with no ownership check. Confirms the exact defect, files, line range, and recommendation in the finding.

Verified directly. schema/quickbooks.ts:40 comment says 4-part format `${iv}:${tag}:${data}:${version}`. Both encrypt() implementations (lib/quickbooks.ts:43 and routes-quickbooks.ts:75) produce exactly `${iv}:${tag}:${ciphertext}` (3 parts, no version), and both decrypt() implementations (lib/quickbooks.ts:48 and routes-quickbooks.ts:80) destructure only 3 parts via split(':'). The comment is stale relative to the code in this slice. Severity LOW matches the finder's own assessment — documentation-only drift, no functional bug in the 3-part functions themselves.

Verified against actual code. legacyUserScopedQuickBooksEnabled() at routes-quickbooks.ts:117-123 exactly as described: single process-wide ENABLE_LEGACY_USER_SCOPED_QB_SYNC env var, no per-tenant/school flag, defaults true when NODE_ENV==='test' unless explicitly set to 'false'. Confirmed it gates 10 call sites across the legacy auth-url/callback/sync/disconnect endpoints (lines 173, 213, 346, 395, 730, 769, 817, 843, 872, 914, 1035), so the blast radius claim (all schools/users simultaneously) is accurate. Severity LOW is appropriate: routes are additionally behind requireAdmin/requireSuperAdmin, and the finder itself frames this as low-likelihood/config-risk rather than an active vulnerability.

Verified both claims directly. (1) src/lib/schema/quickbooks.ts line 92: atosEntityIdx uses Drizzle's index() builder, not uniqueIndex()/.unique() — produces a plain non-unique btree index despite the line-91 comment claiming 'composite unique enforces one mapping per ATOS entity per school'. No DB-level uniqueness on (flightSchoolId, atosEntityId, atosEntityType). (2) qbEntityMapRepo.insert() (lines 126-165): calls findLegacy() (a SELECT, lines 167-187) then conditionally does a bare .insert() with no ON CONFLICT clause and no transaction/advisory-lock wrapping the check+insert together — genuine check-then-act race. Two concurrent inserts for the same entity can both pass findLegacy before either commits its insert, producing duplicate qb_entity_map rows. Note beyond the finder's report: insert() first calls externalReferencesRepo.upsertReference() (line 130) against a newer 'external_references' table — qb_entity_map appears to be a legacy table being phased out (metadata: {legacyTable: 'qb_entity_map'}, function named findLegacy). This doesn't invalidate the finding (the claims about qb_entity_map's own constraint and race are accurate as stated) but does mean the newer upsertReference path may carry the actual production safety guarantee — worth the recommendation acknowledging this rather than only patching the legacy path. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: real defect, requires a genuine race window to trigger, and blast radius is somewhat bounded by qb_entity_map being the superseded/legacy table rather than the primary sync mapping.

findings.title: Instructor 'View Students' popup fuzzy-matches classes by substring name, risking cross-instructor student data exposure
findings.detail: In the useEffect that loads students for the 'View Students' popup (location-instructors.tsx:561-630), classes are matched to the selected instructor via cInstructor.includes(nameLower) || nameLower.includes(cInstructor) || (c.instructorId || '') === studentsPopupInstructor.id (line 587-591). The substring fallback matches run alongside the exact instructorId match, not only when instructorId is missing. A code comment two functions earlier (lines 405-407, for checkride pass-rate stats) explicitly calls out this exact hazard: 'Match checkride history exclusively by instructorId to prevent cross-contamination between instructors who share the same name' - but the fuzzy-name fallback for the students popup was never removed or guarded the same way.
findings.impact: Two instructors with the same or overlapping name (or one name a substring of another) will have their classes cross-matched, causing one instructor's roster to display another instructor's students in an admin-facing popup - a student-data scoping leak across instructor accounts within a school.
findings.recommendation: Match classes to the instructor by instructorId only; remove the substring includes() fallback, or restrict it to a last-resort path only when instructorId is entirely absent on the class record.

findings.title: Deleting a training plan template has zero confirmation and autosaves immediately
findings.detail: The trash-can button in the templates list (location-training-plan-templates.tsx:3889-3896) calls deleteTemplate(template.id) directly on click with no confirm dialog, no ConfirmDrawer (the codebase's own established pattern for the sibling certificate/ratings tab), and no window.confirm. deleteTemplate (line 2242-2247) calls applyTemplateChange, which invokes onChange, wired in location-settings.tsx to handleTrainingPlanTemplatesChange (location-settings.tsx:4148), which immediately PUTs the filtered template list to /location-config/:locationId - an unconditional autosave with no client-visible undo path.
findings.impact: A single misclick permanently and instantly deletes a training plan template representing potentially significant configuration work, with no confirmation step to catch the mistake before persistence.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the delete action in the existing ConfirmDrawer component before calling deleteTemplate.

findings.title: Deleting a qualification type has zero confirmation before the DELETE request fires
findings.detail: The delete button for each qualification type (location-qualifications-catalog.tsx:551-562) calls handleDelete(qt) directly on click. handleDelete (line 265-294) immediately fires a DELETE request with no confirmation UI. The server sometimes soft-disables instead of hard-deleting, but the user has no way to know this before clicking.
findings.impact: An admin can remove a qualification type from the school's catalog with a single accidental click and no way to cancel.
findings.recommendation: Add a confirm step (native confirm() at minimum, or the shared ConfirmDrawer) before calling handleDelete.

findings.title: Instructor CRUD actions hardcode _auditUser: 'Admin' instead of the real logged-in user
findings.detail: handleAddInstructor, handleEditInstructor, handleArchive, and handleReactivate (location-instructors.tsx:691,768,809,851) all send _auditUser: 'Admin' as a literal string, even though the component already destructures the real logged-in user via useAuth() (line 254) and never uses it for this field. Server-side, routes-locations.ts:10128-10129 persists _auditUser verbatim into the audit-log entry's actor field.
findings.impact: Every instructor create/edit/archive/reactivate action is recorded in the audit trail as done by a generic 'Admin' rather than the actual admin who performed it.
findings.recommendation: Replace the literal 'Admin' with authUser?.name || 'Admin', matching the correct pattern already used in location-settings.tsx.

findings.title: Custom expiration-months input in Qualifications Catalog unmounts itself after the first keystroke
findings.detail: When a user selects 'Custom...' from the expiration-rule dropdown (location-qualifications-catalog.tsx:632-663), a numeric input for custom months renders only while form.expirationMonths === 'custom' (line 649), with onChange setting form.expirationMonths to the typed digits but no value prop. As soon as the user types the first character, form.expirationMonths becomes the typed string, the === 'custom' check becomes false, and the custom input unmounts; the select also has no matching option for the typed value.
findings.impact: It is impossible to enter a custom expiration period in months via this form - the input disappears after one keystroke.
findings.recommendation: Track the custom months value in a separate state field distinct from the select's 'custom' sentinel, and only fold it into the saved expirationMonths payload at save time.

findings.title: Silent partial-failure when a course offering's total-events edit cascades to linked training programs
findings.detail: saveAvailableCourse (location-training-certificates-ratings.tsx:1047-1109) recalculates and PUTs updated courseOrder to every training program referencing the edited course using Promise.allSettled, but never inspects the settled results for rejections/failures. The function proceeds straight to a success toast regardless of whether any per-program PUT actually succeeded.
findings.impact: If one or more affected programs fail to update, the admin sees only a generic success toast with no indication a program's course order is now out of sync.
findings.recommendation: Check Promise.allSettled results for rejections/non-ok responses and surface a warning toast listing which linked programs failed to update.

findings.title: ACH fee preview formula diverges from the shared processing-fee calculation used for the card fee preview
findings.detail: The card-fee preview (location-settings.tsx:5333-5338) routes through the shared calculateProcessingFeeCents helper. The ACH-fee preview (5347-5350) instead hand-rolls (100 * Math.max(0, achProcessingFeeValue || 0)) / 100, which simplifies to just achProcessingFeeValue - numerically correct only because the sample transaction is fixed at exactly $100.
findings.impact: No live user-facing bug today, but the formula is fragile: any future change to the sample amount or to calculateProcessingFeeCents's rounding logic will silently desync the ACH preview from the card preview.
findings.recommendation: Replace the hand-rolled ACH formula with calculateProcessingFeeCents({ subtotalCents: 10000, feeType: settings.achProcessingFeeType, feeValue: settings.achProcessingFeeValue }) / 100.

findings.title: Invalid Tailwind class translate-x-5.5 breaks the settings-toggle thumb animation on school-settings.tsx
findings.detail: The custom toggle switch at school-settings.tsx:429 uses translate-x-5.5 for the 'on' state of its thumb. This is not a standard Tailwind spacing value and does not appear anywhere else in the codebase - every other toggle switch consistently uses translate-x-5.
findings.impact: Tailwind will not generate a matching utility for translate-x-5.5, so the toggle thumb likely fails to visibly slide to the 'on' position.
findings.recommendation: Change translate-x-5.5 to translate-x-5 to match every other toggle in the codebase.

findings.title: Location Audit Log page derives locationId by string-splitting the URL path instead of using the route param
findings.detail: LocationAuditLogPage (location-audit-log.tsx:155-163) ignores useParams() and instead splits location.pathname, finds the index of the literal string 'location', and takes the next path segment as locationId. It currently works only because in both mounting route shapes the segment right after 'location' happens to be the id.
findings.impact: Fragile: any future route restructuring will silently break locationId resolution with no compile-time warning.
findings.recommendation: Use useParams<{ locationId: string }>() (falling back to activeLocation?.id) instead of manual path parsing.

result.note: All cited lines verified exact: L3 hardcoded default secret, L21-23 isProductionRuntime() checks only NODE_ENV (no VERCEL_ENV), L25-27 isServerE2eAuthBypassEnabled() gate, L35-37 getE2eAuthBypassSecret() ?? fallback, L58-71 getE2eAuthBypassUser() defaults to role:'super_admin' when no user cookie.
