Verified against routes-auth.ts lines 1547-1588. The endpoint hashes and writes the new password directly to authAccount with no call to auth.api.revokeUserSessions and no mustChangePassword flag. Confirmed this breaks an established codebase pattern: revokeUserSessions is called in the same file at lines 730 (create-user-temp-password), 1357 (grant-super-admin), 1491 (verify-credentials), and 1871 (revoke-super-admin) — all with the same 'revoke stale sessions' rationale in comments. emergency-password-reset is a requireSuperAdmin()-gated endpoint explicitly commented as for emergency/incident use (likely account compromise), so leaving existing sessions alive defeats its purpose. Severity HIGH is appropriate given the security-incident-response context and directly analogous precedent already in the file.

Verified at src/server/routes/routes-auth.ts lines 298-333. SELECT existingAdmins (301-305) and the createUser INSERT (322-331) are two separate, non-transactional DB operations with no row lock or unique constraint preventing concurrent bootstrap. TOCTOU race is real: two concurrent unauthenticated POSTs can both pass the length>0 check before either createUser commits, each becoming super_admin. Severity LOW is correct — narrow one-time setup window, requires precise concurrent timing, no ongoing exploitability once first admin exists.

Verified at routes-ai-schedule.ts:3470-3486 — performedByUserId/performedByName taken directly from request body with no cross-check against c.get('authUser'), while sibling audit writers in the same file hardcode the performer. Severity MEDIUM is correct (requires admin auth already; impact is limited to audit-trail attribution integrity, not data access).

Verified against actual code. Lines 2792 (PUT) and 2839 (DELETE) in routes-locations.ts both call requireAuth() with no options argument. In auth.ts:153-169, the role-check block is gated by `options?.roles?.length` — when roles is undefined (as here), the check is skipped entirely and any authenticated user of any role passes. Both handlers correctly scope by orgId (flightSchoolId !== orgId -> 404) but perform no role/permission check before allowing rename (PUT) or soft-delete via status='inactive' (DELETE, confirmed at line 2855 calling mvpRepository.locations.delete). requireAdmin() is confirmed in use elsewhere in the same file (e.g. lines 2516, 2609, 2653, 2708) for comparable admin-gated operations, corroborating the inconsistency claim. Severity HIGH is appropriate: this is a real privilege-escalation gap allowing any low-privileged authenticated org member (student/instructor) to take down or corrupt a school's location record, a business-critical operation elsewhere gated to admin.

Verified against actual code. Route handler at routes-ai-schedule.ts:3574-3683 matches exactly. The insert loop (lines 3621-3634) iterates record.proposedScheduleJson.events and inserts into schedule_events with zero conflict/capacity/operational-hours checks and no db.transaction wrapper. Confirmed /publish (line 729, tx at 812) and /publish-selected (line 1201, tx at 1290) both use db.transaction for their insert loops, unlike this confirm endpoint. isEntityFree/entityHoursOnDate guard functions exist (defined 2185/2205) and are used by solver logic elsewhere in the file, supporting the comparison claim. Severity HIGH is appropriate — a booking-integrity gap (double-booking, no rollback on partial failure) affecting live scheduling data.

Verified against src/server/routes/routes-ai-schedule.ts. isEntityFree (line 2196), entityHoursOnDate (2215), and entityEventCount (2230, 2233) each compare only slot.entityId, never slot.entityType. Confirmed entityType is populated on pushed slots (e.g. lines 2154, 2161). Notably studentLessonsOnDate (line 2248) DOES check both entityId and entityType, showing the pattern is known/used elsewhere in the same block but inconsistently applied — supports the finding's characterization as an unenforced invariant rather than a fundamental design gap. Severity LOW is correct: exploitability requires a UUID collision across entity types, which is cryptographically negligible under standard UUID generation, so no active correctness bug — genuinely a defense-in-depth/latent-assumption issue as described.

Verified in code. src/server/middleware/auth.ts:153-179 requireAuth(options?: {roles?: string[]}) — when roles is omitted, any authenticated user (any role) passes, only 401 on missing/invalid session. grep confirms routes-locations.ts: 262 bare requireAuth() calls, 14 requireAdmin() calls, 0 requireSuperAdmin(), 0 requireAuth({roles:...}) usages — matches the finding's 262/14 split exactly (274 vs 276 total raw hits is a trivial counting variance, immaterial). Spot-checked mutating routes gated only by bare requireAuth(): PUT /locations/:id, DELETE /locations/:id, PUT /location-config/:locationId, POST .../programs, .../courses, .../equipment, .../students, .../schedule, .../customers — all confirmed reachable by any authenticated role with no role gate. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: it's a breadth/pattern finding, properly hedged as non-exhaustive, and correctly framed as compounding with (not duplicating) the separate tenant-isolation finding.

Verified against actual code. resolveFlightSchoolFromLocation() (line 2963) resolves flightSchoolId from locationId but its docstring's claimed invariant ("every caller compares the result to the session orgId") is false. Spot-checked 7 of the cited call sites and all confirm the pattern: GET /locations/:locationId/customers (39793), GET /locations/:locationId/payroll (37475, requireAuth only), GET /locations/:locationId/admins (40336, requireAuth only), GET .../payment-cards (23400), POST .../force-document-upload (26666, requireAdmin but still no org check), POST /locations/:locationId/notifications (42723, requireAuth). Each only checks isUuid(locationId) and flightSchoolId non-null (location exists) -- never resolveOrgIdFromSession + flightSchoolId !== orgId comparison. Confirmed contrast: sibling POST /locations/:locationId/customers (39834) correctly does resolveOrgIdFromSession -> findByIdUnscoped -> loc.flightSchoolId !== orgId -> 404, proving the guard pattern exists and is simply omitted on the ~58 call sites using the unscoped resolver. This is a genuine cross-tenant PII/financial/compliance data leak (payment cards, payroll, admin roster, documents, logbooks, audit trails) plus two write-path vulnerabilities. Severity CRITICAL is correct as given -- no downgrade warranted.

findings.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can read/write any other student's LMS progress and guide assignments
findings.detail: Every studentId-parameterized route in routes-lms.ts is gated by requireAuth() only, with no ownership check or flightSchoolId scoping, and the repository layer trusts the caller-supplied studentId directly. Vulnerable endpoints: POST /lms/progress (line 1008), GET /lms/progress/:studentId/:courseId (line 1157), GET /lms/guide-assignments/student/:studentId (line 1366), GET /lms/guide-assignments/count/:studentId (line 1452), POST /lms/guide-assignments/:assignmentId/complete (line 1579), POST /lms/questions (line 750, studentId spoofable in body). The sibling Hilo University system resolves the caller's own users.id server-side for every progress operation; this file does not.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user, including a student, can view another student's course completion data, forge progress/completion updates for another student, mark another student's assignment complete, and post questions impersonating another student. No multi-tenant boundary at all.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the caller's own Hilo users.id server-side and use it as the authoritative studentId for self-service routes; require requireAdmin() plus flightSchoolId scoping for admin/instructor views, mirroring routes-hilo-university-analytics.ts.

findings.title: PUT /admin/lessons/:lessonId writes to a Postgres GENERATED column and will 500
findings.detail: hiloUniversityLessons.isPublished is a Postgres STORED GENERATED column (schema/index.ts:11194). PUT /hilo-university/admin/lessons/:lessonId (routes-hilo-university.ts:1632-1633) still writes updates.isPublished = body.isPublished when provided, which Postgres rejects. The typed client wrapper adminUpdateLesson() still advertises isPublished as a valid field. The current UI no longer sends isPublished (publish state now routes through the newer publish/unpublish/archive endpoints), so this is dormant but armed for any future caller following the documented contract.
findings.impact: Any caller supplying isPublished to this endpoint gets a hard 500 from an unhandled Postgres generated-column write error.
findings.recommendation: Remove isPublished from the PUT handler and from the adminUpdateLesson() TypeScript payload type; reject it defensively with a 422 if present.

findings.title: Lesson prerequisites are stored and cycle-checked but never enforced for learner access
findings.detail: routes-hilo-university-authoring.ts implements full prerequisite CRUD with cycle detection, but the learner-facing GET /lessons/:lessonId/full and POST /steps/:stepId/complete never query hiloUniversityLessonPrerequisites -- confirmed by an explicit code comment 'No prerequisite gate.' at line 837. The frontend warning banner is explicitly warn-only, never blocks.
findings.impact: A student can complete a lesson without ever touching its declared prerequisites; the authoring feature has no functional effect on the learner path.
findings.recommendation: Either add a server-side prerequisite-completion check to the learner read/write paths, or document that prerequisites are intentionally advisory-only.

findings.title: Silent catch blocks in LMS pages violate the project's explicit no-silent-empty-state convention
findings.detail: lms-instructor-inbox.tsx:50 uses .catch(console.error) leaving questions as [] with the empty-state UI shown on fetch failure. lms-dashboard.tsx:136 uses .catch((err) => console.error(...)) leaving stats null with all tiles silently showing 0. lms-dashboard.tsx:151 uses .catch(() => {}) with no logging at all for the at-risk widget.
findings.impact: Users cannot distinguish a failed fetch from a genuinely empty state -- instructors think there are no pending questions, admins see a dashboard silently reporting zero stats.
findings.recommendation: Add toast.error(...) and/or a loadError state rendering a distinct error UI, matching the correct pattern already used in hilo-university-home.tsx and lms-courses.tsx.

findings.title: N+1 query pattern hydrating LMS questions with course/lesson titles
findings.detail: GET /lms/courses/:courseId/questions (line 667-694) does a per-row async title lookup inside Promise.all instead of a join, while the sibling GET /lms/questions already does this correctly via findQuestionsWithJoin() (line 712-714).
findings.impact: Extra DB round trips scale linearly with question count on a per-course basis.
findings.recommendation: Replace the per-row lookups with a single joined query filtered by courseId, mirroring findQuestionsWithJoin().

findings.title: hilo_university_lesson_progress.completed_at defaults to now() on insert, not on actual completion
findings.detail: completedAt is .notNull().defaultNow() (schema/index.ts:11279), so it is stamped when a learner starts a lesson, not when they finish it. Two separate route files already have to special-case this by gating output on status === 'completed' (routes-hilo-university.ts:419, routes-hilo-university-analytics.ts:386-389).
findings.impact: Any new query reading completedAt directly without checking status will misreport an in-progress lesson as completed at start time.
findings.recommendation: Make completedAt nullable with no default and set it only on the write path that transitions status to completed. This is a schema change requiring explicit user approval per the Destructive Action Guard.

findings.title: Client-side draft-hiding for students is cosmetic only -- server returns all courses including drafts
findings.detail: lms-courses.tsx:135 filters drafts client-side for students, but GET /lms/courses (routes-lms.ts:102) applies no status filter and returns every course to any requireAuth() caller.
findings.impact: A student calling the API directly can see draft/unpublished study guide titles and descriptions.
findings.recommendation: Add server-side role-based filtering to GET /lms/courses so students only receive published courses.

Verified against actual code. handlePublishIntent (ai-schedule-sandbox.tsx:2948-2996) blocks publish client-side on scopedConflictCount>0, incomplete reviewChecklist, and missing overrideReason when needsOverrideReason is true — exact match to the finding. A direct authenticated admin API call can publish conflicting/unreviewed draft events. Verified against src/lib/training-plan-allocation.ts. All three functions (applyHoursToActiveTrainingPlanCourse L233-241, manuallyActivateNextTrainingPlanCourse L357-365, advanceTrainingPlanAfterCheckride L469-477) share the exact pattern: `Number.isInteger(requestedIndex) ? clamp(...) : Math.max(0, courseAllocations.findIndex(a => a.status === 'active'))`. When no allocation is 'active', findIndex returns -1 and Math.max(0,-1)=0 silently selects index 0 regardless of its actual status. Confirmed 4 live call sites of applyHoursToActiveTrainingPlanCourse in routes-locations.ts (lines 11446, 19985, 20081, 20290). Severity HIGH is appropriate — silent data corruption (wrong course credited hours) with no error surfaced, feeding financial/FAA-hour-tracking downstream consumers.

Loop sums definitionTotalCents and adds each definition's amount unconditionally to the matched certificate's fees (line 142) before the check. Only the itemAmountCents > definitionTotalCents branch (145-147) exists; there is no else-branch handling definitionTotalCents > itemAmountCents (no scaling, no flag, no cap). Over-allocated definition rows flow straight into allocatedFeeCents/feeAmount/totalAmount uncorrected. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate.

Verified both sites via Read. training-plan-course-schedule.ts:77-82 getLocalDateOnly() uses date.getFullYear()/getMonth()/getDate() (local server timezone getters). training-plan-payment-schedule-view.ts:107-108 getStatus() inlines the identical local-getter pattern. parseDateOnly (course-schedule.ts:5-10, confirmed via grep) anchors stored date-only strings to UTC midnight via 'T00:00:00.000Z' before comparison. So local 'today' is string-compared against UTC-anchored date strings exactly as described -- in a server timezone behind UTC (e.g. US timezones), this can misclassify course/payment status (upcoming/scheduled/due/overdue/past_target) by hours around UTC midnight. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate: real correctness bug affecting user-facing billing/schedule status, but bounded to a narrow window near day boundaries, not data loss or security. Duplication across two files is also confirmed as claimed.

Verified at src/lib/training-plan-quote-data.ts lines 141-150: sumBucket computes instructionHours (category !== 'aircraft') and equipmentHours (category === 'aircraft') separately, then returns Math.max(instructionHours, equipmentHours) with no equality check or discrepancy logging. Silent-masking/observability defect, not a functional correctness bug today — severity LOW as finder assessed.

Verified directly against curriculumBuilder.ts. The 'generate-curriculum' step.run (lines 109-185) has no try/catch; createFunction config (lines 59-66) has retries:0 and no onFailure handler. Any throw inside (AI gateway not configured at line 111, safeParseAIJson failure, invalid stages at 153-157, or callClaudeStreaming error) propagates uncaught with zero retries, leaving the DB row at status:'building' (set line 100) forever — only 'completed' (line 193) is ever written, no code path sets 'failed'. Confirmed the cited sibling pattern too: curriculumEnricher.ts lines 193-208 wraps its risky step in try/catch, sets status:'failed' + error message, then rethrows — exactly the missing pattern. Severity HIGH is correct: clear, easily-triggered failure mode (any Claude API error) with a real user-facing symptom (perpetual spinner per doc comment near routes-ai-curriculum-builder.ts:651-655), and no auto-recovery since retries:0.

Verified against actual code. Lines 405-412 of training-plan-allocation-adjustments.ts pair nextItems[index] with previousItems[index] by raw array position — no id/key check beyond a flat groupSourceId equality per item. Confirmed sole caller at routes-locations.ts:12938-12940 passes storedHourItems as previousItems and pricingImpact.hourItems as nextItems. No runtime assertion on previousItems.length === nextItems.length or matching groupSourceId/bucket per pair exists in the function. Severity LOW is appropriate: it's a real unenforced invariant / latent footgun for a future caller, not a currently-triggered defect — the finding correctly hedges impact as a 'plausible' future risk, not an active bug.

Verified both regex implementations exactly as described: routes-ai-curriculum-builder.ts:578-583 uses anchored `^```...```$` (multiline) regex; lib/import/helpers.ts:413-420 uses non-anchored `/```(?:\w+)?\n?([\s\S]*?)\n?```/` specifically to tolerate preamble text. Severity MEDIUM is appropriate as given.</note>

Verified against source: lines 1020-1024 in the debounced autosave effect only console.error + return on !res.ok, no toast/UI feedback. Verified at src/server/routes/routes-ai-curriculum-incremental.ts lines 595-598, 600, 611-612. Only upper-bound check exists (`stageIdx >= outline.stages.length`); no lower-bound check. A negative stageIdx (e.g. -1) passes the guard, `outline.stages[stageIdx]` evaluates to undefined, and accessing `.name`/`.description` on it inside buildStagePrompt throws, causing an unhandled 500 instead of the intended 400. Endpoint is behind requireAuth so exploitability is limited to an authenticated malformed-input DoS/error-spam scenario, consistent with LOW severity as finder rated. Both POST /curriculum-export/generate (lines 289-302) and POST /curriculum-export/revise-page (lines 566-584) destructure `curriculum`/`module` directly from the request body with no DB lookup by ID scoped to orgId. Any authenticated user can submit an arbitrary curriculum/module shape and get AI generation run against it. Verified against actual code. GET /:buildId (465-488), approve-outline (496-547), generate-stage (556-664), approve-stage (672-734) all filter only by id+flightSchoolId, no userId check — matches finding exactly. Verified at routes-ai-curriculum-builder.ts lines 202-237. Verified against actual code. Route is behind requireAuth(), so this is an authenticated-user data-quality/DX issue, not an unauthenticated attack surface — LOW severity is correctly scoped (wastes a build slot + API call, doesn't corrupt data or crash the server).

Verified against actual code. Verified against src/server/routes/routes-parts.ts lines 594-707 (finding cited 594-694, actual block runs to ~707).
